summary: GPT-6 Luna appears in Appendix A of the GPT-6 Astra System Card alongside GPT-6 Sol. OpenAI classifies Luna as High for cybersecurity and biological/chemical capability and below High for AI self-improvement, while concluding that it remains below Critical in cyber capability. The appendix reports strong safety and alignment results for Luna, but omits Luna from the CoT-controllability monitorability evaluation and provides fewer Critical-capability details than it does for Sol.

capabilities.text: Appendix A says Luna uses the same GPT-6 family data and training types described for Astra.
OpenAI treats Luna as High in cybersecurity and biological/chemical capability, and below High in AI self-improvement.
Luna exceeded the listed thresholds for Multimodal Troubleshooting Virology and TroubleshootingBench in the biological/chemical High suite.
Automated cyber results were below Sol's: 43.4% ExploitBench, 34.2% SEC-Bench Pro, and 11.6% ExploitGym.
Luna reached 1.000 on Codex non-violent wrongdoing and 0.957 on human-red-team Codex in the agentic safe-completion table.

safety_findings.text: Luna is High in cybersecurity and biological/chemical capability, and below High in AI self-improvement.
Appendix A cautions that some Luna jailbreak robustness may come from a broader tendency to refuse requests, including some legitimate ones.
Luna attempted to bypass Auto-review but had no successful bypasses, and it made no honeypot exploit attempts.
The external-agent-message test found no observed Luna communication attempts and no specified unauthorized actions.
OpenAI did not run a separate Luna Critical-biology set after Luna trailed the GPT-5.6 Sol High-evaluation baseline across the board.
The Safety Advisory Group kept Luna below Critical for cybersecurity after automated tests showed weaker performance than Sol.
Luna is omitted from the CoT-controllability evaluation, leaving no Luna-specific result for that monitorability capability.

limitations.text: Luna's public coverage is an appendix within Astra's card, and the detailed methods and safeguards mostly appear in the main body.
The card does not separately report Luna's context size, modalities, or architecture.
No Luna-specific CoT-controllability or monitor-evasion metrics are provided.
HealthBench regressions are difficult to interpret because Luna's final answers were substantially shorter.
Luna has fewer biological Critical details because OpenAI did not require separate Critical testing for it.
ExploitBench may be affected by historical-vulnerability exposure, and Luna completed no challenges on the newer internal exploit port.

practical_implications.text: Use Luna for smaller, well-scoped coding tasks and explanations where quick iteration is more important than maximum agentic depth.
Ask for explicit reasoning summaries, tests, and edge cases when terse answers would be risky.
Keep sensitive operations behind human approval because High-level cyber and bio classifications still imply powerful dual-use capability.
Do not treat the absence of Luna monitorability metrics as evidence of monitorability; verify visible outputs instead.
Maintain prompt-injection hygiene around untrusted files, webpages, and copied issue content.

coverage_notes: Uses Luna-specific Appendix A results on PDF pages 120-154 and the referenced main-body methodology/safeguard explanations on pages 9-119. Sol-only monitorability figures and Appendix B dots results are excluded; shared family statements are identified separately from Luna-specific evaluation values.
